question.text: A foreign pension fund is evaluating participation in 'Ganga Credit Opportunities AIF' via a Mauritius feeder. The sponsor explains that pooling offshore contributions outside India offers a specific compliance efficiency. What is that efficiency?

answer.text: The offshore pool is automatically exempt from Indian income-tax on all capital gains
Each offshore investor is automatically treated as Accredited Investor under SEBI rules
The offshore pool bypasses the need to register under either FPI or FVCI Regulations
Only the offshore Fund needs a PAN and to file Indian tax returns, not each of the offshore investors individually

explanation.text: The Logic: When offshore investors are pooled outside India, PAN and Indian tax-return-filing obligations apply only to the offshore fund vehicle, not to each underlying investor — a meaningful compliance saving for the LP base. The Trap: Option A conflates compliance efficiency with tax exemption — pooling does not waive Indian tax. Option B misreads the Accredited Investor framework. Option C is false — applicable FPI/FVCI registration is still required. Note: The compliance benefit attaches to pooling outside India; pooling inside India does not deliver the same PAN/return-filing relief.
